name: Autosomal Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2C

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CMT2C

criteria.description: Presence of distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly in lower limbs with sensory loss
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with reduced compound muscle action potentials
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the TRPV4 gene
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Lack of demyelinating features on nerve conduction studies differentiating from CMT1

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of distal neuropathy symptoms with electrophysiological confirmation of axonal neuropathy plus identification of pathogenic TRPV4 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis due to phenotypic overlap with other CMT subtypes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy of lower limbs

searchTerms: reduced feeling in hands and feet
loss of sensation in fingers and toes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Vocal cord paresis leading to hoarseness
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic feature distinguishing CMT2C from other CMT types
searchTerms: hoarse voice from weak vocal cords
voice changes due to vocal cord weakness

common.symptomName: Mild distal sensory neuropathy with impaired vibration sense
searchTerms: mild numbness with poor vibration sense
slight loss of feeling in hands and feet
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

occasional.symptomName: Hoarseness due to vocal cord paralysis
searchTerms: voice hoarseness from vocal cord paralysis
difficulty speaking due to vocal cord weakness

laboratory: Nerve biopsy may show axonal degeneration
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Laryngeal electromyography may demonstrate vocal cord dysfunction
other: Nerve conduction studies showing reduced amplitude with normal or mildly reduced conduction velocities consistent with axonal neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Demyelinating neuropathy with slowed nerve conduction velocities

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness and sensory loss
Respiratory insufficiency or respiratory muscle weakness
references: Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(10):562-571.
